title: Cantina Ortaccio Vecchi Filari
about: Cantina Ortaccio is the tiny natural-wine project of Massimo “Max” Antonuzi and his partner Patrizia Montanari in Latera, a village above Lake Bolsena in remote northern Lazio, close to the Tuscan border. Max’s family has lived here for generations; he trained as an architect in Rome and ran a wine bar there from 2003 to 2013 before leaving to make wine himself, starting in 2015. The cellar sits directly beneath the couple’s house. It is a very small, little-documented producer, and much of what is known comes from the importers and shops that carry its wines.

Vecchi Filari means “old rows,” and the wine comes from small parcels of old, nearly forgotten vines on volcanic soils at around 400–500 metres. The blend is roughly 45% Sangiovese, 45% Greghetto and 10% Ciliegiolo. The vines are farmed organically, the grapes ferment spontaneously on their own yeasts in fibreglass without temperature control, and the wine is aged in old oak and chestnut barrels. It is bottled unfined and unfiltered, with no added sulphur.

In the glass this is a rustic, honest red from the hills of Tuscia, with retailers describing plum and black cherry with earthy and eucalyptus notes. Recent bottlings have come in at about 13% alcohol. Like Ortaccio’s Dritto Bianco, the skin-contact Procanico also on our list, it is a wine of place rather than polish, and it suits food from the wood fire.
facts: Natural red: spontaneous ferment, unfined, unfiltered, no added sulphur
